#### 1. cerebral arteriopathy, autosomal dominant, with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy, type 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.779)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9013508, Reactome:R-HSA-1912399, Reactome:R-HSA-1912420, Reactome:R-HSA-9017802, Reactome:R-HSA-1912408)

Gain-of-function variants in NOTCH3 lead to aberrant Notch signaling, manifesting differently in familial partial lipodystrophy, Kobberling type (subcutaneous fat loss) and cerebral arteriopathy, autosomal dominant, with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy, type 1 (leukoencephalopathy and cerebral small vessel disease).

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in NOTCH3 that cause familial partial lipodystrophy, Kobberling type via loss-of-function mechanisms, or variants in other genes that are the sole cause of either disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome or genome sequencing data showing that common variants (AF > 0.01) in NOTCH3 are associated with either disease would also challenge the rare variant hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NOTCH3 in these distinct neurological and metabolic disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for interventions aimed at modulating Notch signaling, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
